clue.text: She has pain from one side to the other

indicators.note: the two sides hold the pain between them, so 'has' signals one piece containing the other

parts.note: R, right, is one side
L, left, is the other side
an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: Someone suffers an ache that spreads right across their body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From one side to the other' gives R and L, right and left; 'has' puts ACHE between them. 'She' as the definition simply asks for a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Rachel is a woman's given name, so it can stand for a female person referred to as 'she'.

parts.note: reads like things collapsing, but these are folded sheets opened out that show you the route to take

explanation.definitionFit: Road maps are folded charts that are opened out to show a driver which route to follow.

parts.note: suggests a medic's stack of vinyl discs, but means the file in which a physician keeps notes on patients

explanation.definitionFit: A physician's casebook is the volume of written notes on patients treated, a gathering of medical histories.

indicators.note: only part of the word conversed is wanted, so 'some' tells us to look for a run of letters within it

explanation.surface: A few people chatted together in an old Celtic tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes a run of letters from inside 'conversed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is an old name for the Gaelic language of Scotland or Ireland.

clue.text: In distribution of income the company is thrifty

indicators.note: a distribution spreads things around, so the letters of these words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
CO is the usual abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A firm that shares out its earnings carefully is careful with money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distribution of' rearranges INCOME together with CO, the abbreviation for company.
explanation.definitionFit: Economic can mean economical, sparing in spending and avoiding waste.

clue.text: Moses received them in order, ten set out in writing

parts.note: a command is an order

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit inside the abbreviation, as 'in writing' suggests

parts.note: MS, manuscript, is a piece of writing

indicators.note: laid out afresh, so the letters of ten are rearranged

explanation.surface: Moses took his tablets in sequence, the ten written down one after another.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' is only a link; the second 'in' is the container signal, and 'set out' means rearrange. MS stands for manuscript, a common abbreviation for writing.
explanation.definitionFit: On Mount Sinai Moses was given the Ten Commandments, God's laws carved on stone tablets.

indicators.note: the word night loses its final letter, as 'without end' suggests

explanation.surface: Darkness that never finishes, very nearly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without end' drops the last letter, T, from 'Night'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigh is an old word for near, so it serves as nearly or close to.

indicators.note: ploughing turns the soil over, so the letters of a mowed are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: A field that was cut for hay is then dug over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ploughed' is the signal to rearrange A MOWED.
explanation.definitionFit: A meadow is a grassy field, often kept for hay.

indicators.note: sent off the wrong way, so the letters of traces are put in another order

explanation.surface: Tracking marks sent the wrong way lead to delivered stores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrongly directed' rearranges TRACES. 'Supplies' is the verb: provides food or services.
explanation.definitionFit: To cater is to provide food or services, so the verb sense matches providing.

clue.text: Give rating a note to take between ships

indicators.note: the note is held between the ships, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the abbreviation for a ship; plural ships gives it twice
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A sailor is assessed and handed a message to carry between vessels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ships' gives two lots of SS, steamship; 'to take between' places the note E between them, all after A.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess is to evaluate or put a value on something, the same as grading it.

clue.text: He's bound to better himself elsewhere

definitions.text: He's bound to better himself elsewhere

parts.words: He's bound to better himself elsewhere
parts.note: 'bound' reads as certain to, but means heading for: a person setting off to a new country hoping for a better life

explanation.definitionFit: An emigrant leaves his homeland to settle abroad, usually seeking improved prospects.
The phrase means both moved forward and, of a suitor, tried to begin a romantic relationship.

clue.text: Gangs require a doctor qualified in surgery

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
BS, Bachelor of Surgery, is a surgical qualification

explanation.surface: Criminal gangs need a trained surgeon on hand.
explanation.walkthrough: MO is medical officer; BS is the degree Bachelor of Surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: Mobs are disorderly crowds or criminal groups, like gangs.

indicators.note: out of place, so the letters of a lad's are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boy has been dismissed in cricket, perhaps bowled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' rearranges A LAD'S. In cricket a batter who is 'bowled' is out, but here 'bowled' means served in a bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: A salad is a dish typically served in a bowl, so it is something that may be bowled.

clue.text: Animal with fur and a round head

parts.note: a boa is a long fur stole

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of round

explanation.surface: A creature with a furry coat and a big round head.
explanation.walkthrough: A BOA is a long scarf of fur or feathers; 'head' takes the first letter of 'round'.
explanation.definitionFit: A boar is a wild or male pig, an animal.

parts.note: F, forte, is the musical direction for loud
ire is anger

explanation.walkthrough: F is forte, the musical marking for loud.
explanation.definitionFit: Afire means on fire, burning brightly.

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards, so the word for nobleman goes backwards

parts.note: a lord is a nobleman
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: An entertaining aristocrat reaches fifty years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns LORD upwards to DROL, then L, Roman fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: Droll means wryly funny, entertaining in a dry way.

clue.text: They use first impressions to eradicate the wrong types

definitions.text: They use first impressions to eradicate the wrong types

parts.words: They use first impressions to eradicate the wrong types
parts.note: sounds like people judging others at first meeting, but 'impressions' are trial printings and 'types' are printed characters to correct

explanation.definitionFit: Checkers of printed galleys use early copies to find and fix mistaken characters before publication.

clue.text: This canine is a biter on sight

indicators.note: one piece comes on, after, the other

parts.note: the eye is the organ of sight
a tooth is something that bites

explanation.surface: This dog bites whenever it sees you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canine' looks like a dog but is the pointed tooth; 'on' here means coming after.
explanation.definitionFit: The eye tooth is the canine tooth in the upper jaw, below the eye.

definitions.meaning: money taken from a sale or event, as a noun

explanation.definitionFit: Proceeds as a verb means goes forward; as a noun it means money raised, the takings.

clue.text: Two things required for a fiddle at the card table

definitions.text: Two things required for a fiddle at the card table

parts.words: Two things required for a fiddle at the card table
parts.note: suggests cheating at cards; read as a violin, it needs a support for its strings and a musician, while the joined term names a card game participant

explanation.definitionFit: A violin needs a bridge and someone to play it; together the words name one who plays the card game bridge.

parts.note: sounds like having no clean garments left, but means dashing about naked in public

explanation.definitionFit: To streak is to run naked through a public place, as pranksters at sports matches do.

clue.text: Tie for which the Football Association needs nets put up

parts.note: FA is the Football Association, English football's governing body

indicators.note: in a down clue putting up means reading upwards, so nets is read backwards

explanation.surface: Football officials need goal nets hung up and secured.
explanation.walkthrough: FA is the Football Association; 'put up' turns NETS upwards to STEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To fasten is to secure or bind, as tying does.

indicators.note: turning round reverses the word for leave

parts.note: to part is to leave

explanation.surface: A car swings round and drives off.
explanation.definitionFit: A trap is a light two-wheeled carriage pulled by a horse.

clue.text: Either way you can play it

definitions.text: Either way you can play it

parts.words: Either way you can play it
parts.note: read forwards it is a pub game; read backwards it is the short name for a Stradivarius violin, which you also play

explanation.definitionFit: Darts is a pub game; written backwards it gives STRAD, a Stradivarius violin, also played.

clue.text: Duck gets twitching in the ear

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O
a tic is a twitching of a muscle

explanation.surface: A duck develops a nervous twitch in its ear.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a cricket score of zero, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: Otic is the medical adjective for things relating to the ear.

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.walkthrough: P is piano, the musical marking for soft.
explanation.definitionFit: A wasp is an insect that buzzes.

clue.text: Lord of high standing and narrow outlook

definitions.meaning: a noble of rank in the House of Lords
to look closely through narrowed eyes

explanation.definitionFit: A peer is a noble with a title; to peer is to squint closely at something.

definitions.meaning: to delight or carry away with emotion, a verb

explanation.definitionFit: An entrance is a way in; to entrance, stressed on the second syllable, is to enchant or enrapture.

definitions.meaning: to look good on, as clothing flatters someone

explanation.definitionFit: Become means both to flatter, as a dress does its wearer, and to turn into.

parts.note: read literally it is the monarch's own letters; really a vertical roof timber, so a support

explanation.definitionFit: A king post is the central upright timber in a roof truss; whimsically, a monarch's letters.

clue.text: They may have fallen on peoples' feet

definitions.text: They may have fallen on peoples' feet

parts.words: They may have fallen on peoples' feet
parts.note: suggests things dropped onto toes, but means the curved undersides of feet that can sag, as in flat feet

explanation.definitionFit: Fallen arches are a foot condition in which the curved instep flattens.
